messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated DNS error rate for api.eu.redwood.example — multiple SERVFAIL/FORMERR observed from Cloudflare resolver cluster. probes fired 03:07 UTC. auto-page to oncall

Morgan: oncall here. acknowledging. paging Tyler, Anya, Luis. What metrics are we seeing?

Tyler: seeing spike in backend 5xx from eu edge loadbalancers starting ~03:05. Digging into gateway logs shows DNS lookup timeouts and downstream upstream errors. Funnel shows ~9% of EU traffic failing name resolution.

Anya: any recent GeoDNS or Route53 policy changes? Also are we sure this is upstream resolver behaviour and not our authoritative zone misconfig?

Luis: quick checks from a handful of public resolvers and our probes:
```bash
# london probe (1.1.1.1)
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.eu.redwood.example A +short
199.51.100.10

# frankfurt probe (1.1.1.1)
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.eu.redwood.example A
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @1.1.1.1 api.eu.redwood.example A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 57821
```
Direct queries to our Route53 NS return normal A records. So authoritative seems fine. Recursor pool (Cloudflare) returning intermittent SERVFAIL and some truncated UDP responses.

Morgan: support has inbound tickets reporting embeddings failures for some EU customers. Estimate impact: 7-12% of EU requests erroring due to DNS resolution issues.

Tyler: Runbook suggests doing a GeoDNS traffic shift to fallback region while provider investigates. Anya, can you approve a short TTL and weight change? We want eu-fallback to take primary for ~30 minutes.

Anya: approved. Luis, please prepare change batch and execute. Keep TTL low (30s) and annotate the change. Also notify customers.

Luis: prepping Route53 change (sample payload included in ticket). Plan: set eu-primary weight 0, eu-fallback weight 100, TTL 30. Will submit via aws cli.

Tyler: submitting now. Will post change-id.

devops-bot: Route53 change submitted, change-id C-20260315-01. Status: PENDING.

Morgan: switching synthetic probe cadence to 20s for EU. Also re-ran resolver sampling across multiple public providers (1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1, 8.8.8.8, and Cloudflare's anycast clusters).

Luis: some probes now show stable answers, but a subset of Cloudflare edge resolvers in eu-central still give truncated responses (TC=1) causing recursors to fail fallback to TCP in some networks. Captured small pcap and attached to ticket.

Tyler: Route53 change now INSYNC (C-20260315-01). Switching LB routing to prefer eu-fallback. Watching error rate...

support-bot: customer notification posted to affected tickets. Link: https://support.redwood/INC-4289. Short message sent: investigating DNS errors affecting EU region, temporary failover in place.

Tyler: after the failover we see API 5xx drop to baseline for most customers, overall EU error rate down from ~9% to ~1.2% within 90s. Good mitigation.

Anya: open a ticket with Cloudflare account team and include dig samples, packet captures, timestamps, and affected resolver IP ranges. Might be an internal caching/edge problem. Luis, can you open that?

Luis: opened CF ticket #CF-2026-1337. Attached query samples and pcap. CF asked for timestamps and example resolver IPs — forwarded.

Tyler: logging note: avoid overly aggressive TTL changes in future; some recursors ignore short TTLs and continue serving stale or cached negative answers. Add to postmortem.

devops-bot: automated health checks: no unexpected route churn detected, CDN static hit ratio at 80%, queue depth within normal limits.

Morgan: placing incident in watch-mode. Oncall coverage: Morgan primary until 06:00 UTC. Escalate if EU DNS error rate >3% for 10m or any high-profile customer impact.

Anya: tracking actions in Jira INFRA-4327. Assignments: Luis (cloud comms + artifacts), Tyler (runbook update + verification tests), Morgan (postmortem draft). Target: initial postmortem in 48h.

Luis: uploaded pcap and resolver probes to the Jira ticket and linked CF case CF-2026-1337. CF replied: investigating a regional resolver software upgrade that may have introduced a bug; they will confirm whether RRL or rate-limiting rules triggered our SERVFAILs.

support-bot: status page update published: https://status.redwood/incident/2026-03-15-dns-eu. Customer-facing note: temporary DNS instability in EU resolved via failover; CF investigating root cause.

Tyler: small operational suggestion — add a cross-resolver synthetic check (compare answers from 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, and our NS) and automatic failover trigger if discrepancy > 5% for 2 consecutive minutes. Will add to runbook.

Morgan: thanks all. Closing active paging. Will reopen if any regression. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT MOVED TO WATCH-MODE. last alert observed 03:43 UTC. Incident duration ~36 minutes.
